# Testing · project standards (detail)

<!-- docs/standards/testing.md · Generated by project-init v0.4.1 on 2026-11-17, updated by v0.9.0 on 2026-11-19.
On-demand reference: not loaded automatically. The short rules Claude follows are in .claude/rules/testing.md. -->

## Test shape: a pyramid
- **Rule:** Most tests are fast unit tests on pure domain logic. Fewer tests cover the pipeline and the provider adapters (against saved real responses), and only a few `AppTest` tests cover whole user journeys.
- **Why:** Most of this app's rules (scoring, RACI, recalculation, state) are pure logic, so that's where most bugs can be caught cheaply.
- **Decision:** Pyramid rather than a mostly-integration "trophy", because the logic lives in plain Python and Streamlit's `AppTest` journeys are slower and coarser.
- **Status:** Adopting. The folders already follow it (`tests/unit/`, `tests/llm/`, `tests/ui/`).

## Tests with the code
- **Rule:** Every change ships with tests. Every bug fix starts with a failing regression test. Domain logic is written test-first.
- **Why:** Untested changes are guesses.
- **Decision:** Test-first for domain logic. Tests written after the code are fine for UI work, as long as they ship in the same change.
- **Status:** Tests-with-every-change is documented in CLAUDE.md. Test-first and regression tests are Adopting.

## Positive, negative and boundary cases
- **Rule:** For each behaviour, test the normal case, one invalid input per kind (empty, wrong format, too long, out of range, special characters) and each limit and just past it. A negative test asserts the specific error or rejection, not just that nothing crashed.
- **Why:** Most escaped bugs live in invalid input and edge values, not on the happy path.
- **Status:** Normal, boundary and failure cases are documented in CLAUDE.md. The specific-assertion habit is Adopting.

## Failure paths of dependencies
- **Rule:** For each external dependency, simulate its failures with a fake or a recorded response: timeout, connection error, rate limit, error response, malformed or schema-invalid output. Assert that the app fails clearly, retries only where intended, and never shows a key, stack trace or raw provider error.
- **Why:** Providers fail regularly. An untested failure path turns a provider hiccup into a crash or a leak.
- **Status:** Enforced for the Claude client (`tests/llm/`). Adopting for any new dependency.

## Exploratory test sessions
- **Rule:** Before each release, run a chartered, time-boxed session ("Explore <area> with <technique> to discover <risk>", 60 to 90 minutes) and write a short debrief: what was covered, what was found, what is still open. Each finding becomes an issue and then a regression test. At least one session is done by a person, for user-experience judgment. Claude may run sessions too, in demo mode only (no paid calls, no real keys), and reports findings without fixing them in the same session.
- **Why:** Scripted tests only check the risks someone thought of. Exploration finds the others, and the regression tests keep them from coming back.
- **Status:** Planned for Release v0.1.

## Tests gate merges
- **Rule:** CI runs the full suite on every push and pull request, and feature branches reach `develop` only with CI green.
- **Why:** A test that blocks nothing is eventually ignored.
- **Status:** Enforced in CI. Whether branch protection blocks the merge on GitHub is not checked here.

## Coverage as a signal
- **Rule:** Track coverage and keep a floor of 80% on `domain`. Don't write tests only to raise the number.
- **Why:** Low coverage shows risk; chasing 100% produces low-value tests.
- **Status:** Planned for M8.

## Security tests in the pipeline
- **Rule:** Run static security analysis and dependency vulnerability scanning on every pull request.
- **Why:** Finds known vulnerability patterns early and automatically.
- **Status:** Static analysis is enforced (ruff's `S` rules, gitleaks). Dependency scanning is planned for M6 ([#69](https://github.com/io-sar/ai-generated-project-troubleshooter/issues/69)).

## Smoke tests after deploy
- **Rule:** Run the manual smoke and timing checks in the roadmap before each release.
- **Why:** Catches a broken deploy before visitors do.
- **Decision:** Kept the roadmap's manual checks. Streamlit Community Cloud deploys from GitHub with no post-deploy hook or automatic rollback.
- **Status:** Kept current (ROADMAP: Release v0.1 and v1.0).

## Flaky tests
- **Rule:** A test that fails intermittently gets an issue and is fixed or deleted. Never re-run until green as a habit.
- **Why:** Flaky tests teach people to ignore red builds.
- **Status:** Adopting.
